extracted.intended_audience: aristocratic women and courtiers (readers of Renaissance courtly etiquette)
extracted.subtask_short: court lady etiquette in Renaissance court
extracted.subtask_description: Norms and standards for the behaviour, appearance, accomplishments, and conversation of a Court Lady at a Renaissance court, as argued in Castiglione's Third Book of The Courtier. Focuses on virtues, social graces, appropriate bodily exercises, dress, and conversational skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Womanly difference in manners and bearing
rubrics_metrics.description: A woman ought to be very unlike a man: she should show 'a soft and dainty tenderness with an air of womanly sweetness in her every movement' so that in going, staying, or saying what she will she 'shall always make her seem the woman, without any likeness of a man.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: adopting 'stout and sturdy manliness' is unbecoming. Emphasize gentleness and distinctively feminine deportment in gestures and bearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared classical virtues with the Courtier
rubrics_metrics.description: Possess the same virtues taught to the Courtier — 'prudence, magnanimity, continence, and many others' — which are valuable both in private governance (household, children) and in public behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: these virtues should not be relegated to menial household tasks only; they should also inform conversation and graceful practice of bodily exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid negative character traits
rubrics_metrics.description: Be naturally graceful and avoid affectation; be mannerly, clever, prudent, not arrogant, not envious, not slanderous, not vain, not quarrelsome, not silly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: cultivate gentle birth (to avoid affectation) and disposition that 'wins and keeps the favour of her mistress and of all others.' Anti-patterns: vanity, slander, quarrelsomeness, and affectation reduce respect and esteem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain beauty and guard reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty is especially necessary to a woman; she should be circumspect and take great care not to give occasion for evil to be said of her, avoiding even suspicion because 'a woman has not so many ways of defending herself against false imputations as has a man.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: act so as to escape not only guilt but even suspicion. Anti-pattern: behaviour that invites gossip or ambiguous situations that could be misread.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleasant affability and adaptable conversation
rubrics_metrics.description: Possess a 'certain pleasant affability' enabling her to entertain politely 'every sort of man with agreeable and seemly converse, suited to the time and place, and to the rank of the person with whom she may speak,' combined with calm, modest manners and quick vivacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance modesty and wit so as to appear both agreeable and virtuous; preserve a mean — touch limits without passing them. Tailor topics, tone and vivacity to interlocutor's rank and setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid extremes of coyness or over-familiarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not be so coy as to seem to abhor company (which may suggest concealment), nor so free as to utter unseemly words or practice wild, unbridled familiarity; when present at free talk, listen with a blush and shame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-patterns: excessive prudishness (which appears affected) and crude familiarity (which invites bad reputation). The recommended posture is modest restraint and appropriate blush/shyness in certain company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not gossip about other women
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid saying or willingly listening to evil about other women; prying into and narrating others' intrigues suggests envy and leads men to hold such women in small respect and even despise their company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: lively recounting of unseemly tales; such behaviour invites being seen as envious, loquacious, and morally suspect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate gravity tempered with wisdom and goodness
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibit a gravity (tempered by wisdom and goodness) that acts as a shield against insolence; 'a word or laugh or act of kindness (however small it be) from a virtuous woman is more prized by everyone' than the endearments of shameless women.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: modest, virtuous demeanour commands respect and is more effective socially than ostentatious flirting or shamelessness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be well-informed and choose conversational topics carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Words that carry no meaning of importance are vain and puerile' — the Court Lady must have knowledge of many things in order to entertain graciously; she should choose topics adapted to the quality of her interlocutor and guard against inadvertently offending him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid praising oneself indiscreetly, prolixity, mixing serious with playful discourse, and pretending knowledge of what one does not know; modestly display real knowledge to do herself credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perform feminine-appropriate bodily exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Women should practise bodily exercises becoming to them: in dancing avoid too active or violent movements; in singing/playing avoid abrupt, oft-repeated diminutions that show more skill than sweetness; avoid playing harsh instruments (drums, fifes, trumpets) whose harshness destroys mildness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: execute dance and music circumspectly, with gentle daintiness and a touch of shyness to display 'noble shame.' Anti-patterns: vigorous, manly exercises (handling weapons, wrestling) or harsh musical timbres.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt dress to enhance grace while avoiding vanity
rubrics_metrics.description: Adapt garments to the intent and to the exercises planned, choosing clothes that enhance her grace and are appropriate to the moment; correct bodily imperfections covertly while always seeming 'to give no thought or heed to it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: wear attire that enhances natural gifts (cheerful style for cheerful beauty, serious fashions for gentle/serious style), but avoid seeming vain or frivolous; remain dainty and neat but unconcerned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquire appropriate accomplishments (letters, music, painting, dance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be acquainted with letters, music, painting, and know how to dance and make merry; also possess at least an understanding of exercises she does not practise so she may praise and value cavaliers according to their deserts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: these accomplishments enable graceful entertainment and proper valuation of others' merits; a minimal intellectual acquaintance is acceptable where practical mastery is not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adorn oneself with classical virtues beyond entertainment
rubrics_metrics.description: Possess continence, magnanimity, temperance, strength of mind, prudence and other virtues — not merely for entertainment but so she 'may be full of virtue' and 'worthy of being honoured' and that every act be governed by them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: virtues are ends in themselves and reinforce social respect; they should inform conduct even when not visibly required for diversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation in claimed abilities — avoid impossible perfection
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not ascribe to the Court Lady impossibly many virtues or knowledge of 'all the things in the world'; it suffices to be 'beautiful, discreet, chaste, gracious, and able (without incurring infamy) to entertain with dancing, music, games, laughter, witticisms.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: extravagant or false praise and claims of universal knowledge appear absurd and are counterproductive; prefer credible, moderate praise of attainable qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperament and prudence valued over rash bravery
rubrics_metrics.description: Timidity or cautiousness in women springs from subtlety and readiness of wit and can be praiseworthy; true loftiness comes from deliberation and determined resolve, not foolhardy ignorance of danger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: prudence and measured deliberation are higher virtues than reckless bravery; being discerning and cautious is socially and morally valuable.
